name: Kennedy Space Center Launch
company: NASA / Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
unique: Watch a rocket leave the pad across the Indian River, then stand under an actual Saturn V, the only place you can do both in one day.
buzz: Launch days are transcendent and traffic is apocalyptic; the visitor complex alone is a full day. Buy launch-viewing tickets the day they drop.

name: Swim with Manatees
unique: In winter, hundreds of West Indian manatees crowd the warm springs, and you can snorkel beside them in clear water while they sleep, eat lettuce and ignore you.
buzz: Operators are strictly regulated and good ones brief you on no-touch rules; visibility depends on the tide. Book the earliest boat.

name: Dry Tortugas and Fort Jefferson
unique: A hexagonal brick fort on a tiny island 70 miles from Key West, surrounded by clear water and coral, reachable only by boat or seaplane.
buzz: People call it the best day trip in Florida; the ferry is long and expensive and the snorkeling is the reward. Book weeks ahead.

name: National Naval Aviation Museum
unique: One of the largest naval aviation museums in the world, with Blue Angels jets, a World War II carrier deck and a flight simulator, free on a naval base.
buzz: Free and enormous, with planes you can walk around and climb into. Bring ID for base access.

name: Blue Spring Manatees
unique: A first-magnitude spring that becomes a winter refuge for hundreds of manatees, viewable from a boardwalk in water so clear you can count the scars on their backs.
buzz: On a cold January morning there can be 300 manatees; arrive at opening because the park fills by 9am. Swimming is closed in manatee season.

name: Edward Ball Wakulla Springs State Park
dates: Year round, boats on a schedule
unique: One of the largest and deepest freshwater springs in the world, with glass bottom boat tours over a riverbed of mastodon bones, manatees in winter, alligators, and a 1930s lodge with hand painted ceilings where Creature from the Black Lagoon was filmed.
buzz: The boat tour is the thing to book and the rangers call out manatees and turtles. The lodge and the swimming area are from another era and the water is cold and clear enough to see the bottom.

name: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge
unique: A full-scale Star Wars outpost where the cast never breaks character, you can build a lightsaber in a secret workshop and fly the Millennium Falcon with five strangers.
buzz: Rise of the Resistance is the best ride in America by acclimation; the lines and the upcharges are the cost. Rope-drop or buy the lightning lane.

name: T.H. Stone Memorial St. Joseph Peninsula State Park
unique: Nine miles of undeveloped barrier peninsula with dunes twenty feet high, a bay side calm enough for small children and a gulf side with clear green water, plus a campground behind the dunes that books eleven months out.
buzz: People who know it call it the best beach in Florida and it stays quiet because there is nothing to buy there. The campground reservation is the hardest part and the bay side is where families with small children go.

name: Wynwood Walls
unique: A warehouse district turned open air mural museum, with monumental pieces by Shepard Fairey, OSGEMEOS and friends, surrounded by galleries, breweries and a decade of gentrification.
buzz: Worth the ticket for the curated courtyard; the surrounding streets are free and just as good. Go before noon for photos and fewer crowds.

name: Salvador Dali Museum
unique: The most comprehensive Dali collection outside Spain, in a hurricane-proof glass bubble on the waterfront, with massive canvases that reward standing close.
buzz: The building and the collection are both stunning; the free audio guide is genuinely good. Go Thursday evening for the smaller crowd.

name: Apalachicola Historic District
unique: A working waterfront town of Greek Revival cotton warehouses, sponge docks and oyster houses on the Apalachicola River, where the commercial fishing fleet still unloads and the streets behind it are a national historic district.
buzz: The oysters are the reason people come and the town is the reason they stay. It has kept its scale, and the raw bars on Water Street serve what the boats brought in that morning.

name: Bahia Honda State Park
unique: A state park on a keys island with a sand beach, a historic bridge ruin, snorkeling and campsites on the water.
buzz: The beach is one of the best in the keys and the old bridge is the photo. Book camping months ahead.

name: Bok Tower Gardens
unique: A 250 acre garden on a hill with a 205 foot Singing Tower, a carillon that plays daily and a pine forest that feels like Georgia.
buzz: The tower and the carillon concert are the reason, and the gardens are cool and quiet. Go for the afternoon recital.

name: Corkscrew Swamp Sanctuary
unique: A 2.25 mile boardwalk through an old growth cypress swamp, with alligators, otters and the largest nesting colony of wood storks in the country.
buzz: The boardwalk is flat and the swamp is genuinely wild. Go in winter for the birds and bring water.

name: Devil's Den Prehistoric Spring
unique: A karst window into a 54-foot deep spring under a collapsed roof, with fossil beds in the walls, sunbeams through a hole in the ceiling and 72-degree water.
buzz: Snorkelers love the cathedral light; it is small and gets crowded, so book a morning slot. Not for claustrophobic swimmers.

name: Dr. Julian G. Bruce St. George Island State Park
unique: Nine miles of undeveloped gulf beach at the end of a barrier island, with dunes, sea oats, a campground in the scrub and a bay side marsh where migratory birds drop in by the thousand in spring.
buzz: Campers book the sites a year ahead and birders come in April for the migration. The beach is wide and empty compared to the developed end of the island.

name: Fort De Soto Park
unique: A county park on five keys with a fort, a beach that regularly ranks among the best in the country, a dog beach and a ferry to Egmont Key.
buzz: The north beach is the calm one and the fort is a bonus. Parking is cheap and the sand is white.

name: J.N. Ding Darling National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A mangrove refuge on Sanibel with a wildlife drive, wading birds, alligators and a visitor center, one of the best birding spots in Florida.
buzz: The drive at low tide is the best time, and the roseate spoonbills are the prize. Bring bug spray.

name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
unique: The first undersea park in the country, with coral reefs, a sunken statue garden and snorkel and dive boats leaving from the marina.
buzz: The snorkel trip is the reason to come, and the reef is shallow enough for beginners. Book ahead in season.

name: Morikami Museum and Japanese Gardens
unique: A Japanese garden and museum built around a 1900s farming colony, with a tea house, koi ponds, bonsai and a taiko drum festival.
buzz: The gardens are genuinely serene and the museum explains the Japanese settlement of Florida. The bonsai collection is excellent.

name: Pensacola Beach
unique: A barrier island beach of sugar white sand and emerald water, with a pier, a boardwalk and the Blue Angels practicing overhead.
buzz: The sand is the best on the Gulf and the water is clear. Parking costs in the main lots.

name: Ringling Museum
unique: A circus magnate's Venetian Gothic mansion, a 21-gallery art museum and a circus museum with the actual train car and wardrobe of the greatest show on earth.
buzz: The circus museum is the surprise hit with kids; the house tour and grounds are gorgeous at sunset. Ticket bundles are worth it.

name: Siesta Key Beach
unique: A wide beach of quartz white sand that stays cool underfoot, with a lagoon, volleyball courts and a drum circle on Sundays.
buzz: The sand is the story and the sunset drum circle is the local ritual. Parking fills early.

name: St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Seventy thousand acres of coastal marsh, pine flatwoods and impoundments along the Big Bend, with a seven mile drive to an 1842 lighthouse, wintering ducks by the thousand and the best migration birding in north Florida.
buzz: The lighthouse at the end of the drive is the photograph everybody takes and the impoundments in winter are full of birds. Alligators sun on the levee roads and photographers come for the fall migration.

name: Torreya State Park
unique: Bluffs above the Apalachicola River that rise more than a hundred and fifty feet, the steepest hiking in Florida, with the rare torreya tree, a 1930s CCC built stone lodge and a view of river swamp that looks like mountains from the top.
buzz: Hikers say it is the only place in Florida that feels like a mountain state and the climb out of the ravine is real. Botanists come for the endemic trees and the fall color is the best in the panhandle.

name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
unique: A 1916 Italian Renaissance villa on Biscayne Bay, built by an industrialist with European rooms, formal gardens and a stone barge breakwater.
buzz: The house and the gardens are equally good, and the bay terrace is the photo. Go early before the tour buses.

name: Skydive Zephyrhills
customer: First timers, young adults, bucket listers
unique: One of the largest drop zones in the world, with a 14,000-foot tandem jump over flat Florida farmland and the Gulf beyond, no mountains, just the horizon.
buzz: Tandem instructors get consistent praise for calming nerves; video packages are worth it. Weather delays are common in summer.

name: Anna Maria Island
unique: A seven mile barrier island of white sand, a wooden pier, a village of cottages and a free trolley that runs the length of it.
buzz: The trolley makes it easy without a car, and the beach is wide and calm. Sunsets at the pier are the ritual.

name: Apalachicola Bluffs and Ravines Preserve
dates: October to April, guided and reserved access
unique: The Garden of Eden Trail drops off the bluff into steephead ravines where cool seeps keep plants that survive nowhere else, down to the Apalachicola River and back up, on land managed to restore the longleaf and ravine forest.
buzz: The climb back out is the hardest mile in the panhandle and the ravines are genuinely strange for Florida. Access is by reservation and the quiet is part of the deal.

name: Blackwater River State Park
unique: A sand bottomed river running clear and amber through longleaf pine flatwoods, with white sand bars for stopping, a swimming area and a campground, on a designated state paddling trail that runs for miles.
buzz: Paddlers call it the best family river in the panhandle because the current is gentle and the sand is white. On summer weekends the put in fills by nine.

name: Castillo de San Marcos
unique: The oldest masonry fort in the continental United States, built from coquina shell stone that absorbed cannonballs, on the oldest continuously occupied European street grid in the country.
buzz: Rangers fire cannons on weekends; the walls are fun to climb and the history is brutal and well told. Combine with the old town at dusk.

name: Circle B Bar Reserve
unique: A 1,200 acre former ranch turned wetland preserve with a boardwalk, oak hammocks and alligators everywhere, one of the best wildlife walks in central Florida.
buzz: The alligators are close and the birds are abundant. Go early and stay on the path.

name: Daytona International Speedway
unique: The 2.5 mile superspeedway where NASCAR's biggest race runs, with a track tour, a museum and the banked turns you can walk on.
buzz: The track tour is the way to feel the banks, and the 500 is the bucket list event. Book tours ahead.

name: Everglades Airboat
unique: A flat-bottomed fan boat skims a sawgrass river at 40mph, stopping for alligators, herons and the strange silence of the actual swamp.
buzz: Coopertown is the oldest operator and gets praise for real guides; the souvenir-photo upsell is universal. Bring ear protection for kids.

name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
unique: Eighty three acres of tropical plants, with a rainforest, a butterfly conservatory, a palm collection and a tram tour.
buzz: The butterfly house and the tram are the easy wins, and the collection is world class. Hot in summer, so go early.

name: Florida Caverns State Park
dates: Year round, tours daily on the hour
unique: The only Florida state park with dry cave tours open to the public, where a ranger walks you through limestone chambers of stalactites, flowstone and soda straws carved by water draining through the Marianna lowlands.
buzz: The tour is the reason to come and the guides make the geology land. The cave stays cool in summer, the tour sells out on holidays and the campground and trails are the quiet part.

name: Florida Museum of Natural History
unique: A free museum with a butterfly rainforest, fossil skeletons, Florida's native cultures and a giant shark jaw, on the UF campus.
buzz: The butterfly rainforest is the kid hit and the fossils are serious. Free, with a small fee for the butterfly house.

name: Grayton Beach State Park
unique: A state park with dunes, a coastal dune lake, a beach of white sand and campsites under scrub oak, on Scenic 30A.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the towns and the dune lake is unusual. Book camping early.

name: Kingsley Plantation
unique: A sea island cotton plantation with the planter's house and the tabby slave cabins still standing, on a marsh island in the Timucuan preserve.
buzz: The slave cabins are the powerful part, and the ranger talks are excellent. Free.

name: Little Havana
unique: A Cuban neighborhood centered on Calle Ocho, with cigar rollers, ventanitas, domino players at Maximo Gomez Park and croquetas on every block.
buzz: Go hungry and walk Calle Ocho, then sit in the domino park. The cigar shops are happy to show you how it is done.

name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
unique: A sea turtle hospital with tanks of recovering turtles, a surgical suite and nesting beach programs, free to visit.
buzz: The turtles are close and the staff explain the injuries and the nesting season. Free, with a donation suggested.

name: Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A 140,000 acre refuge beside the space center, with a wildlife drive, manatees, alligators and some of the best birding in the state.
buzz: The Black Point drive is the easy win, especially in winter for waterfowl. Bring binoculars and bug spray.

name: Myakka River State Park
unique: One of the oldest and largest state parks, with a canopy walkway, a river boat tour, alligators and a grassy prairie.
buzz: The canopy walk and the boat tour are the two things to do, and the gators are everywhere. Go early.

name: Paynes Prairie Preserve State Park
unique: A 21,000 acre prairie with wild horses, bison, alligators and a boardwalk, plus a sinkhole that once drained a lake.
buzz: The bison and horses are a surprise in Florida, and the observation tower is the view. Bring bug spray.

name: Silver Springs State Park
unique: A first magnitude spring with glass bottom boat tours, kayak rentals and monkeys in the trees, one of Florida's oldest attractions.
buzz: The glass bottom boat is the classic and the spring water is impossibly clear. Kayaking is the better way to see it.

name: St. Andrews State Park
unique: A park on the pass between the Gulf and St. Andrews Bay, with a snorkeling jetty, a shell island ferry and a beach that stays calm.
buzz: The jetty snorkeling is the draw, with fish and clear water. Good for kids.

name: Steinhatchee Scalloping
company: Local marinas and guides at Steinhatchee
unique: A shallow grass flat off the Big Bend where you snorkel for bay scallops in three to six feet of water, then take them back to a dock where somebody will clean and cook them for you.
buzz: Families plan summer vacations around it and the season is short. The river town has no beach, which keeps the crowds down, and everybody comes back with a cooler.

name: Everglades Hovercraft
unique: A hovercraft glides over sawgrass, mud and shallow water where no boat can go, into mangrove tunnels and abandoned clam camps at the edge of the Ten Thousand Islands.
buzz: The ride is smoother and louder than an airboat; reviews say the small-group trips beat the big-tour buses. Bring sunscreen and earplugs.

name: Solomon's Castle
unique: A castle built from scrap aluminum and salvaged stained glass by an artist who lived in it, filled with wooden machines, painted ceilings and a 60 foot replica of a Spanish galleon.
buzz: It is gloriously eccentric and the tour is funny; the boat tour and the restaurant are extras. Worth the drive inland.

name: Anastasia State Park
unique: A state park on a barrier island with a wide beach, dunes, a salt marsh and campsites under oaks, minutes from the old city.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the city beaches and the camping is shaded. Good for a combination history and beach day.

name: Blowing Rocks Preserve
unique: A limestone shoreline where waves blast water through rock holes at high tide, the largest Anastasia limestone outcrop on the Atlantic coast.
buzz: Go at high tide with a northeast wind for the blowholes, and wear shoes on the rock.

name: Chassahowitzka River
unique: A spring fed river with clear water, cypress and mangrove tunnels, manatees in winter and a campground at the launch.
buzz: The paddle is easy and the spring runs are beautiful. Rent a kayak at the campground and go early.

name: Cummer Museum of Art and Gardens
unique: A riverfront museum with European and American painting, porcelain and formal gardens on the St. Johns, with free admission on some days.
buzz: The gardens on the river are as good as the collection, and the free days make it a bargain.

name: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
unique: The winter estates of Thomas Edison and Henry Ford, with their houses, laboratories, a 1929 botanical garden and Edison's rubber research.
buzz: The labs are the interesting part and the banyan tree is enormous. Allow two hours.

name: Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum
unique: The Spanish colonial house where Hemingway wrote in the 1930s, with his furniture, his typewriter and dozens of polydactyl cats descended from his own.
buzz: The cats are the fun and the writing studio is the history. Tours run continuously and are worth the ticket.

name: Mallory Square Sunset
unique: A nightly street festival that exists only to watch the sun go down: buskers, sword swallowers, cats on tightropes and a crowd that applauds the horizon.
buzz: It is touristy and completely charming; locals avoid it and visitors remember it. Get there an hour before sunset for a seat on the pier.

name: Mission San Luis
unique: A reconstructed 17th century Spanish mission and Apalachee village, with a council house, a friary and living history demonstrations.
buzz: The reconstruction is convincing and the staff explain the collision of Spanish and Apalachee life. Good for kids.

name: National Navy UDT-SEAL Museum
unique: A museum on the beach where the frogmen trained, with boats, dive gear, a bin Laden raid exhibit and the history of naval special warfare.
buzz: The artifacts are real and the stories are intense. Good for teenagers and adults.

name: Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge
unique: The first national wildlife refuge in the country, set aside by Theodore Roosevelt to protect pelicans, with a boardwalk and a bird's eye view of the lagoon.
buzz: The history is the story and the birding is excellent in winter. Quiet and free.

name: Ponce Inlet Lighthouse
unique: The tallest lighthouse in Florida, with 203 steps, a keeper's quarters museum and a view of the inlet and the ocean.
buzz: The climb is hot but the view is worth it, and the museum explains the lighthouse keepers.

name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve
unique: A 3,500 acre wetland preserve with a 1.2 mile boardwalk through cypress, ferns and orchids, with otters, herons and alligators.
buzz: The boardwalk is easy and cool, and the wildlife is close. A good break from the beach.

name: St. Pete Pier
unique: A 26 acre pier district with a modern pier head, a beach, restaurants, a playground and a tram, on Tampa Bay.
buzz: The design is the attraction and the sunset is the show. Free to walk, with paid parking.

name: Suwannee River State Park
unique: The confluence of the Withlacoochee and the Suwannee, with bluff trails above the water, a cemetery and earthworks from a Civil War crossing, a boat ramp and a campground in the longleaf pines.
buzz: The bluff trail along the confluence is the hike and the river is the swim. Paddlers use it as a base for the Suwannee and the campground is one of the better ones in north Florida.

name: Vortex Spring
unique: A spring that pumps out millions of gallons a day at a constant sixty eight degrees, with a cavern mouth that drops into a mapped cave system, a dive training platform, a swimming area and a campground on five hundred acres.
buzz: Divers train here because the water is clear and the cavern is accessible, and families swim the basin on the same day. The dive shop and the rules are taken seriously, which is the point.

name: Weeki Wachee Mermaid Show
unique: Women in mermaid tails perform underwater ballet in a natural spring theater, breathing through hoses, since 1947, the last of a vanished genre of roadside attraction.
buzz: It is gloriously retro and the performers are genuinely athletic; the park's river cruise is a nice add. Kids are mesmerized.

name: Ybor City
customer: Young adults, food people, history people
unique: A historic cigar district of brick factories, mutual aid halls and rooster-filled streets, now bars, cigar shops and Cuban restaurants.
buzz: Walk 7th Avenue, watch a cigar roller and eat a Cuban sandwich. Busy and loud on weekend nights.

name: Air Force Armament Museum
unique: A museum of bombs, missiles, guns and aircraft, with a B-52, an SR-71 and a MOAB, on the Eglin base.
buzz: The hardware is impressive and free. Bring ID for base access.

name: Alfred B. Maclay Gardens State Park
unique: A 1,200 acre estate with formal camellia and azalea gardens, a brick walk, a lake and a 1920s house.
buzz: The spring bloom is the reason, and the brick walk is beautiful. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Apalachicola National Estuarine Research Reserve
company: Florida Department of Environmental Protection and NOAA
unique: A nature center on the bay with tanks of live sturgeon, crabs and oysters, a touch tank, a diorama of the estuary and staff who explain how the river, the bay and the barrier islands make one system that produces most of the state's oysters.
buzz: It is free and the live animals are the draw for children. Adults leave understanding why the river's flow matters, which is the point of the exhibit.

name: Bonnet House Museum and Gardens
unique: A 1920s artist's estate between the beach and the intracoastal, with a shell museum, a courtyard and gardens that survived the condo boom.
buzz: The house is eccentric and personal, and the grounds are a green surprise in the middle of Fort Lauderdale. Guided tours only.

name: Cedar Key
unique: A tiny old Florida fishing and clam town on a Gulf island, with a boardwalk, a dock, clam shacks and sunsets over the marsh.
buzz: The clams and the sunset are the reasons, and the town is small enough to walk. Quiet midweek.

name: Deering Estate
unique: A 1920s stone house on Biscayne Bay with fossil beds, a hardwood hammock and a canoe trail through the mangroves.
buzz: The house tour and the nature trail are both good, and the bay is calm for kayaking. Less crowded than Vizcaya.

name: Devil's Millhopper Geological State Park
unique: A 120 foot deep sinkhole with a boardwalk down to the bottom, fern covered walls and a miniature rainforest at the floor.
buzz: The boardwalk down is steep and cool, and the sinkhole feels like another world. Quick and cheap.

name: Harry P. Leu Gardens
unique: Fifty acres of camellias, roses and a tropical rainforest on a lake, with a 1880s house museum and a butterfly garden.
buzz: Shady and quiet, a good break from the theme parks. The camellia collection is the winter highlight.

name: Lafayette Blue Springs State Park
dates: Year round, swimming best May to September
unique: A blue spring that boils up beside the Suwannee River and spills into it over a limestone ledge, with a swimming basin, a boat ramp where the two waters meet and moss hung oaks over both.
buzz: Swimmers like that the basin is small and the river is right there, and divers come for the cave. The park is quiet and cheap and the water is cold year round.

name: Lion Country Safari
unique: A drive through safari park with lions, rhinos, giraffes and zebras loose around the car, plus a walk through amusement area.
buzz: The drive is the fun, especially for kids who have never seen a lion outside a cage. Go early when the animals are active.

name: Naples Pier
unique: A wooden pier on a wide Gulf beach, good for fishing, dolphin watching and the sunset that draws a crowd every night.
buzz: The sunset is the event and the pier is the viewpoint. Parking is tight, so walk or bike.

name: Robert is Here
unique: A fruit stand that became a landmark, selling smoothies from fruit you have never heard of, with a petting zoo, live music and a milkshake list that runs to dozens.
buzz: The smoothies are the reason to stop on the way to the Everglades; the line moves and the exotic fruit tasting is worth it.

name: Seaside
unique: The planned New Urbanist town where The Truman Show was filmed, with pastel cottages, picket fences, a pavilion and a walkable center.
buzz: The architecture is the attraction and the beach is gorgeous. Busy in summer, quiet in winter.

name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
company: St. Augustine Lighthouse and Maritime Museum
unique: A black and white striped lighthouse with a maritime museum and a dark of the moon ghost tour, where staff report footsteps on the tower stairs and a girl in the basement.
buzz: The climb is worth it for the view alone; the ghost tour is one of the better researched ones in Florida. Book after dark.

name: St. Vincent Island National Wildlife Refuge
dates: Year round, daylight; access by boat
unique: A barrier island reachable only by boat with a herd of sambar deer brought from India in the 1900s, loggerhead turtles nesting in summer, and an estuary that serves as a nursery for the bay's oysters and shrimp.
buzz: Birders take the ferry for the shorebirds and the isolation. There are no facilities and no shade, and that is what keeps it empty.

name: Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park
unique: A park on the Suwannee dedicated to the songwriter who never saw the river he made famous, with a carillon tower that plays daily, a museum of Florida folk life and craft demonstrations, and a campground under the oaks.
buzz: The carillon is the thing people remember and the folk life exhibits explain the Cracker culture of the river. It is quiet, cheap and the campground is a local favorite.

name: Superblue Miami
unique: A warehouse of immersive light and sound installations, including a mirrored infinity room and a cloud sculpture you walk through, designed by artists rather than set builders.
buzz: The mirrored room is the photo everyone wants and the timed entry keeps it calm; it is short for the price. Pair with the Design District.

name: Tallahassee Museum
unique: A 52 acre museum of Florida history and wildlife with a 1880s farm, a caboose, a zip line and native animals including panthers and bears.
buzz: The mix of history and animals works for kids, and the zip line is the adrenaline add on.

name: The Florida Aquarium
unique: An aquarium with a walk through wetland gallery, sharks, otters and a coral reef exhibit, plus a splash pad and a penguin encounter.
buzz: The wetland walk through is the best part and the splash pad saves a hot afternoon. Book online for a discount.

name: Winter Park Scenic Boat Tour
unique: A pontoon tour through a chain of lakes and narrow canals, past lakeside mansions and the Rollins College campus, narrated by a local.
buzz: The canals are the charm and the guides are funny. Cheap, shaded and a good break from the heat.

name: Gatorland
unique: A 110-acre alligator park that predates Disney, with a breeding marsh, a boardwalk over thousands of gators and a screaming zipline directly above them.
buzz: It is old Florida and proud of it; the gator wrestling show is a relic and the swamp walk is genuinely good. Cheaper and less crowded than the theme parks.

name: Clearwater Marine Aquarium
unique: A working marine rescue hospital with dolphins, sea turtles and otters, made famous by the Dolphin Tale films.
buzz: The rescue stories are the heart of it and kids connect with the animals. Book tickets online.

name: Coral Castle
unique: A Latvian immigrant single-handedly quarried and moved 1,100 tons of coral rock to build a castle, a rocking chair that weighs tons and a table shaped like Florida, nobody knows how.
buzz: People come for the mystery and leave talking about the loneliness of it; the audio tour tells the story well. Small and strange.

name: Crab Island
unique: A shallow sandbar in the Destin harbor where boats raft up, music plays and people wade in waist deep water, a floating party on the Gulf.
buzz: Rent a pontoon or take a shuttle, bring a cooler and expect a crowd. Not for quiet seekers.

name: Falling Waters State Park
unique: Florida's tallest waterfall, dropping into a hundred foot sinkhole that swallows the creek entirely, with a boardwalk to the overlook, a swimming lake and trails through sandhill and fern covered sinks.
buzz: The waterfall is small by mountain standards and the sinkhole is the story, which the rangers explain. It is a good hour and cheap, and children like the idea of a river disappearing.

name: Flamingo Gardens
unique: A 60 acre botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary with flamingos, a bobcat, otters and a 1930s house, plus a tram through the citrus grove.
buzz: The flamingos and the tram are the kid draw, and the gardens are shady. Good for a hot day.

name: Orlando Science Center
unique: A hands on science center with a giant dinosaur hall, a planetarium, an observatory and a kids zone, in a modern building near downtown.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the planetarium are the hits, and it is a good rainy day alternative to the parks.

name: Ponce de Leon Springs State Park
unique: A spring run where two springs mix and pour sixty million gallons a day into a swimming basin, with a short trail along Sandy Creek, cypress and tupelo overhead and a picnic area under the oaks.
buzz: It is the cheap swimming hole for Holmes County and the water stays at sixty eight degrees year round. Locals go early on summer weekends because the parking lot fills.

name: Sawgrass Recreation Park
unique: An airboat ride into the Everglades with alligators, wading birds and a sawgrass maze, plus a small animal exhibit.
buzz: The airboat is loud and fast and kids love it. The wildlife show is cheesy but the swamp is real.

name: St. Marks Historic Railroad State Trail
unique: Sixteen paved miles on the grade of Florida's first railroad, running from Tallahassee south through the national forest to the old port at St. Marks, where the tracks used to carry cotton to the Gulf.
buzz: It is flat, shaded and free, and the ride into St. Marks ends at a waterfront where the railroad ended. Cyclists do it as a half day and stop for lunch at the coast.

name: Suwannee River at Old Town
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and private campgrounds
unique: A stretch of the Suwannee where the river runs wide and black between limestone banks, with public ramps, riverside campgrounds and sturgeon leaping in summer, which is a real hazard and a real spectacle.
buzz: Paddlers do multi day floats and camp on the banks, and anglers fish for bass and catfish. Locals warn about the jumping sturgeon in summer and everybody has a story about one.

name: Tampa Riverwalk
unique: A 2.6 mile paved trail along the Hillsborough River, connecting the aquarium, the history center, parks and the convention center.
buzz: Flat and scenic, with water taxis and good people watching. Best at sunset.

name: Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks
unique: A Greek-American sponge-diving town with working boats, a cathedral, bakeries selling baklava and a museum of the divers who died harvesting the bay.
buzz: The food is the draw, get Greek salad and grilled octopus on the docks; the boat tours are short and touristy.

name: Blue Springs Recreation Area
unique: A county park on the Chipola River where a blue spring boils up into a swimming area, with a sandy beach, a diving platform, tube floats down the river and a campground in the pines.
buzz: Locals swim here all summer and the tube float is the ritual. It is cheap, the water is cold and the spring is the reason people drive from Dothan.

name: Crystal River Archaeological State Park
unique: A 14 acre mound complex built by the Woodland culture 1,500 years ago, with burial mounds, a plaza and a museum on the river.
buzz: The mounds are subtle but the story is fascinating, and the river setting is pretty. Combine it with a manatee swim.

name: Havana Antique and Vintage Trail
company: Visit Gadsden County and the Havana merchants
unique: A self guided trail through a town that burned in 1916 and rebuilt in brick, now a row of antique shops, design stores and cafes along the main street, in a county that was also the state's shade tobacco capital.
buzz: Dealers say the furniture prices are better than Tallahassee and the town has kept its scale. People come for one shop and spend the afternoon.

name: Jacksonville Beach
unique: A wide Atlantic beach with a pier, surf shops, a boardwalk and a cluster of bars and restaurants, twenty minutes from downtown.
buzz: The pier is the landmark and the surf is consistent. Parking is easier than most Florida beaches.

name: Mount Dora
unique: A hilltop lake town with antique shops, a boardwalk, a historic inn and a steam train, in a part of Florida that has hills.
buzz: The downtown is walkable and the lakefront is pretty, with festivals most weekends in season.

name: Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center
company: Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center
unique: A small center on the barrier island with resident sea turtles that cannot be released, a working rehabilitation space and staff who explain why a plastic bag looks like a jellyfish and what to do with a stranded turtle.
buzz: Children remember the turtles by name and parents like that the message is conservation rather than a photo op. It is small, cheap and close to the beach.

name: Cassadaga Spiritualist Camp
unique: A Victorian camp of mediums and healers in the pine scrub, with a bookstore, a hotel and readings you can book like a haircut.
buzz: Skeptics and believers both enjoy the earnest weirdness; readings vary wildly in quality. Walk the lake at dusk.

name: Cocoa Beach Pier
unique: A 800 foot pier over the Atlantic with restaurants, a surf shop and a view back at the space center launches.
buzz: Good for a walk and a drink, and the surf below is beginner friendly. Parking costs.

name: Forest Capital Museum State Park
unique: A museum on the county that calls itself the forest capital of the south, with a walk through longleaf pine forest, a sawmill display, turpentine stills and a Cracker homestead with a dogtrot cabin and a sugar cane mill.
buzz: The Cracker homestead outdoors is the part children like and the forestry exhibits explain a whole economy. It is cheap, quiet and specific to a place most people drive past.

name: Peace River Wildlife Center
unique: A rehabilitation center for injured birds and small wildlife, with pelicans, owls, eagles and a turtle pond, run by volunteers.
buzz: Small and free, with staff who explain each animal's story. Good for kids.

name: Quincy Historic District
unique: A courthouse square and surrounding streets with one of the largest collections of antebellum and Victorian houses in north Florida, built on the shade tobacco economy that made Gadsden County rich.
buzz: The houses are the attraction and the tobacco history is what explains them. The downtown is quiet and the walking tour takes about an hour.

name: Werner-Boyce Salt Springs
unique: A coastal spring and salt marsh park with a deep spring, paddling trails and a boardwalk, hidden behind the commercial strip.
buzz: The spring is a surprise and the paddle is quiet. Bring bug spray.

name: Blackwater Heritage State Trail
unique: A paved nine mile rail trail from Milton through the old lumber town of Bagdad to the naval air station, on the grade of the Florida and Alabama Railroad, with pine woods and the Blackwater River on either side.
buzz: It is flat, shaded in stretches and free, which makes it the default ride for people in Milton. The Bagdad end has the old mill town houses.

name: Cape San Blas Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse and two keeper's quarters moved off the eroding Cape and rebuilt in town, where you can climb the tower for a view over St. Joseph Bay and read about the hurricanes that forced the move.
buzz: The story of moving the light is as interesting as the climb. Photographers shoot it at sunset and the bay behind it is shallow and glassy.

name: Gadsden Arts Center
unique: A regional art museum and galleries in a restored building on Quincy's square, with changing exhibitions of Florida and southeastern artists and a permanent collection of work by artists with Gadsden County roots.
buzz: The exhibitions change often and the space is better than a town this size usually has. Locals treat it as the cultural anchor of the county.

name: Horseshoe Beach
unique: A fishing village on a hook of land at the edge of the Big Bend, with a boat ramp, a few docks, no high rises and a west facing beach where the sun sets over the marsh instead of the ocean.
buzz: Anglers launch here for the flats and the offshore rocks, and families come for the shallow water and the quiet. It is the kind of Florida town that has not been rebuilt for tourists.

name: Iguanaland and Iguana Fest
unique: A reptile park devoted to iguanas and their relatives, with an annual Iguana Fest of animal encounters and vendors, a niche so specific it becomes a destination.
buzz: Small and earnest; keepers are generous with handling opportunities. The festival is a local street-party vibe rather than a convention.

name: Pine Log State Forest
unique: Florida's first state forest, bought during the Depression, with longleaf pine, a chain of small lakes, a campground and trails for bikes and horses in the sandhills north of Chipley.
buzz: It is quiet, cheap and used mostly by locals with horses and mountain bikes. The lakes fish well and the campground is small enough to feel private.

name: Apalachicola River at Blountstown
dates: Year round, best spring and fall
company: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
unique: A wide, slow stretch of the Apalachicola below the Blountstown bluff, with a public ramp, cypress and tupelo along the banks and a bass and catfish fishery that locals keep to themselves.
buzz: Anglers fish the dead water around the bars and paddlers work upstream against a current that is barely there. There are no facilities, so it stays local.

name: Constitution Convention Museum State Park
unique: A small museum where Florida's first constitution was drafted in 1838, with a walk through exhibit, period rooms and a ranger who will explain why a territory of forty thousand people needed a constitution before it could become a state.
buzz: It is tiny and the ranger makes it. People visiting the coast for the beach are surprised to find the state's founding document was written here.

name: Spook Hill
unique: A gravity hill where you put your car in neutral and appear to roll uphill, with a painted sign and a local legend about an alligator and a pirate.
buzz: It is silly and free and works exactly as promised; kids love it. A five minute stop on the way to Bok Tower.

name: Marianna Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1900s courthouse in the middle and a ring of storefronts, in a town that was a crossroads for both armies and later a peanut and timber market, with antebellum houses on the streets behind it.
buzz: The square is small and the houses around it are the real architecture. People stop on the way to the caverns and find more than they expected.

name: Perry Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a ring of storefronts in a town that has been logging and milling the Big Bend for a century and a half, with the forest products industry still running the county.
buzz: It is a working timber town rather than a tourist one, and the square shows it. People stop for supplies on the way to the coast.

name: Bonifay Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and a few storefronts in the seat of a peanut and cattle county at the top of the state, where the springs are the only reason most people get off the interstate.
buzz: Small, hot and quiet. It is a place to buy a cold drink on the way to Vortex or Ponce de Leon.

name: Chipley Downtown
unique: A small grid of brick storefronts and a courthouse, in a town that grew on the railroad and the turpentine and lumber trade and now sits at the crossroads of two highways with the state's tallest waterfall a few miles south.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of cafes. Most people pass through on the way to the park.

name: Blountstown Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1930s courthouse and a few storefronts a few blocks from the Apalachicola River, in the seat of one of the poorest and least visited counties in Florida.
buzz: Two blocks, one cafe and a river ramp at the end of the street. People pass through on the way to the national forest and the springs.

name: Bristol Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1900s courthouse and a handful of stores in the seat of one of Florida's least populated counties, ten minutes from the bluffs and the river.
buzz: Two blocks and a gas station, and the people are used to hikers buying water. It is the last stop before Torreya.

name: Cross City Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1930s courthouse, a monument and a few stores at the crossroads of the county, in a place built by timber, turpentine and the railroad.
buzz: Two blocks and a diner. It is a stop for ice on the way to Horseshoe Beach or the river.

name: Jasper Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1900s courthouse, a monument and a few storefronts, in a town that sits where the Georgia line meets the Suwannee country and has been a crossroads since the railroad came through.
buzz: Two blocks and a couple of places to eat. It is a stop between the state parks and the interstate.

name: Mayo Courthouse Square
unique: A small square with a 1900s courthouse, a monument and a handful of stores, in one of the smallest county seats in Florida, a few miles from the Suwannee and the blue spring.
buzz: Two blocks and a grocery store, and the people are used to people in wet swimsuits. It is the last stop before the river.
